summary.headline: Inox Wind Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58% QoQ to Rs 1,378 crore, but margin was hit and FY27 revenue guidance was withdrawn.
summary.overview: Inox Wind consolidated revenue rose 58% QoQ to Rs 1,378 crore in Q2 FY27, while adjusted EBITDA was flat QoQ at Rs 238 crore, which management attributed to commodity and raw-material inflation. Management shifted strategy toward equipment supply (target about 75% of third-party order book) and let go of some lower-quality orders, so it declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and conceded it will not hit the earlier growth and margin guidance. Inox Green completed payment and transfer for the Wind World India OEDM portfolio (about 4.5 GW), with consolidation expected from Q3 FY27. Management also announced a CEO change at Inox Wind, with Sanjeev Agarwal resigning and Sai Babu Wattukuri joining as MD of the wind business.

financial_highlights.change: management said would be above 20% had Wind World income been recognised in P&L

segments.name: Inox Wind (equipment and EPC)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 1,378 crore; margin pressured by raw-material and commodity inflation, which management expects to reverse as newly priced orders execute. H1 FY27 order inflow about 1.85 GW; order book about 3.8 GW as of October 2026, about 24 months of visibility.

segments.name: Inox Green (O&M)
segments.commentary: Q2 total income Rs 113 crore, excluding any Wind World income. Portfolio OEDM about 12.5 GW as of September 2026 (10.4 GW wind, 2.1 GW solar). Wind World OEDM consolidation from Q3 FY27; other wind acquisition (about 2 GW) expected by March 2027, subject to approvals.

guidance_outlook: No specific FY27 revenue guidance; management said it will not reach the earlier 75% growth and 20-22% margin guidance for FY27.
FY28 revenue target of about Rs 7,500 crore, to be reviewed toward end of Q4 FY27.
Long-term EBITDA margin objective about 20%, to be judged on an annual basis.
Receivable days expected to fall below 150 days by end of FY28.
Wind World OEDM margin expected to exceed 45% post-integration; Wind World standalone margin of about 25-30% rising to around 40% with value additions, within about 3-4 quarters per management.
Wind World FY26 revenue about Rs 580 crore; Q3 FY27 revenue expected to roughly double the Q2 Inox Green top line, per analyst reconciliation accepted by management.
Consolidation of Inox Green's Power Evacuation business demerger and listing approval expected in the coming one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: 4X wind turbine platform: prototype installed, commissioning expected shortly, commercial launch targeted by end FY27.
Rohika facility in Gujarat dedicated to blades for the 4X platform.
Operational transformer capacity enhanced for 4X series; plans to expand into 8-20 MVA medium transformers and larger units.
Planned manufacture of inverters, unit substations and electronic control systems; investments staged for short payback.
demand_pricing: Equipment supply share of third-party order book about 61% as of October 2026 (target about 75%).
Pipeline of about 5 GW of potential tenders from NTPC, IOC and SECI over the next 4-5 months.
Repeat orders in Q2 from NLC India, Terra Clean Energy (IOC subsidiary) and an IPP.
Management sees no meaningful domestic pricing pressure despite possible new entrants; pass-through clauses apply on many contracts.
India added 1.8 GW wind in Q2 FY27 and 3.2 GW in H1 FY27, vs 6.05 GW in full FY26; MNRE expects 7.5-8 GW wind additions in FY27.
Standalone wind tenders about 2.1 GW of 5.8 GW renewable tenders in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an FY28 order inflow target for Inox Green/Inox Wind?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific order inflow target; management says order book (about 4 GW) covers 2.5-3 years, with focus on free cash flow and balance sheet over order size.

qa_highlights.question: Will the earlier FY27 growth (75%) and 20-22% margin guidance be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not reach those numbers due to the strategy shift and order exits; FY28 guidance seen as conservative and upward-biased.

qa_highlights.question: Will Wind World revenue add about Rs 150 crore to Q3 top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Broadly yes; NCLT approval and transfer agreement signed mid-October, so Q3 top line could roughly double from the Rs 113 crore Q2 base, around Rs 120-150 crore of Wind World revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Inox Green's standalone wind O&M count flat at 3.94 GW while additions are happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone wind additions were made but reflect with lag from commissioning to O&M handover; solar OEDM contracts are being non-renewed for low margins.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the margin and why other income fell?
qa_highlights.answer: No breakdown given; other income fell because Wind World income was not recognised in Q2; other income expected to stay around Q2 levels until consolidation.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing pressure from new entrants such as Adani Wind?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant pricing pressure seen; wind's role in peak hours is rising as solar tariffs weaken.

qa_highlights.question: Inox Wind's Wind World margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone Wind World margin about 25-30% currently, rising to around 40% with value additions, within about 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Ownership and minority interest in Wind World?
qa_highlights.answer: Inox Green owns 75% of Wind World; minority interest will be accounted for in profit line.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on newly priced orders executing; Q2 margin hit by commodity inflation.
Working capital and receivable days (elevated on a half-year basis; management targets below 150 days by end FY28).
Timing of Wind World consolidation (Q3 FY27) and the second wind OEDM acquisition (by March 2027), subject to NCLT and regulatory approvals.
Leadership transition: CEO Sanjeev Agarwal resigned, serving as adviser through December; new MD Sai Babu Wattukuri joined.
Order book reduced by discontinued orders; growth now deliberately slower.
Sustained commodity and raw-material cost inflation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and balance sheet but evasive on FY27 numbers; management repeatedly declined to quantify FY27 and conceded earlier growth and margin guidance will be missed, while asserting that the worst is behind.
key_quotes: We believe the most challenging phase of the transition is now largely behind us.
We believe that the worst is now behind us.
I think we will not reach those numbers what we've guided for.

growth.why: No FY27 revenue guidance was given and management conceded it will miss prior 75% growth and 20-22% margin guidance; FY28 target of ~Rs 7,500 crore is backed only by a ~3.8 GW order book (24 months visibility), a 4X platform launch targeted end-FY27, and Wind World OEDM consolidation from Q3 FY27, with limited quantified capacity behind the FY28 number.

roles: MD of wind business (Sai Babu Wattukuri, joining)
mgmt.note: Sanjeev Agarwal resigned as Inox Wind CEO and Sai Babu Wattukuri joins as MD of the wind business; management has laid out a FY28 Rs 7,500 crore revenue target and equipment-supply shift.
initiatives: Shift toward equipment supply (target ~75% of third-party order book from ~61%)
Wind World OEDM consolidation from Q3 FY27

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects commodity-driven margin hit to reverse as newly priced orders execute; reported EBITDA margin about 17% vs LT objective ~20%, and Wind World OEDM margin expected above 45% post-integration from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 4X platform commercial launch targeted by end FY27 with prototype installed, Rohika blade facility under construction, and Wind World OEDM (about 4.5 GW) consolidating from Q3 FY27; no hard MW capacity addition quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book about 3.8 GW (about 24 months visibility) and FY28 revenue target of about Rs 7,500 crore; Q3 FY27 Wind World revenue of Rs 120-150 crore on a Rs 113 crore Q2 base, but FY27 growth guidance withdrawn and order exits slow growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is being raised in a calibrated way (medium transformers 8-20 MVA, inverters, unit substations) but no capacity or utilisation figure was disclosed, so a major new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it will not reach earlier 75% growth and 20-22% margin guidance for FY27 and gave no FY27 revenue guidance; upside is only framed as FY28 (~Rs 7,500 crore), to be reviewed at end Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Earlier FY27 growth (75%) and margin (20-22%) guidance already conceded as unachievable; raw-material inflation held Q2 EBITDA flat QoQ at Rs 238 crore and receivable days remain above the 150-day target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 4X wind turbine platform commercial launch targeted by end FY27, prototype installed and commissioning shortly.

rows.label: Wind World OEDM consolidation (about 4.5 GW)
rows.why: Payment and transfer completed with NCLT approval; Wind World revenue of Rs 120-150 crore expected to roughly double Inox Green's top line from Rs 113 crore in Q3.

rows.label: Second wind OEDM acquisition (about 2 GW)
rows.why: Expected by March 2027 but subject to approvals, so timing is conditional.

rows.label: Receivable days below 150 by FY28
rows.why: Management targets receivable days below 150 by end FY28, but half-year receivables are currently elevated and no interim path was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term strategy, balance sheet and the Wind World consolidation, but evasive on FY27 numbers and conceded earlier growth and margin guidance will be missed; analysts pressed on FY27 guidance, margins, and pricing pressure from new entrants.

oneOffs.what: Q2 revenue up 58% QoQ to Rs 1,378 crore is a sequential comparison; no one-off item in the revenue base is quantified in the brief

quality.why: Revenue rose 58% QoQ to Rs 1,378 crore while adjusted EBITDA was flat at Rs 238 crore, so the growth did not carry through to profit; the brief attributes the margin squeeze to commodity and raw-material inflation, which means the top-line growth is not clearly price-led either, and the brief does not state the volume or price split of the revenue increase, so the driver is best recorded as price
